metadata.name: two-person-veto
metadata.description: Two of three named people must approve before the write lands, and ONE REJECTION VETOES IT — this is VETO, not quorum: `onBranchError: "fail"` on the quorum join is read before `k` ever matters, so THE FIRST REJECT DECIDES and the run fails with `E_HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, whatever the other two say. The verdict is settled by that rejection; the run itself stays `awaiting_gate` until the other people vote, so a single rejection and silence leaves it parked, not failed. PRODUCT LIMIT — THE VETO CANNOT RECOVER AN EFFECT: the barrier short-circuits on two approvals and the write in `save` runs at once, while the third gate stays open and answerable. A LATE REJECT, arriving after the second approval, therefore fails a run whose write has ALREADY LANDED — the effect stays, and the run is only marked failed; nothing in this graph undoes it. Two approvals are the point of no return, so a person who intends to veto must do it before the second approval. For two-of-three where a lone dissenter is outvoted, copy `two-person-approval.json`, which differs from this file in `onBranchError` and its metadata alone.

labels.reads-as: veto is `onBranchError: "fail"` on a quorum join; `k: 2` buys no tolerance for a dissenter, it only short-circuits the wait for the third person
labels.residue: a short-circuiting quorum join leaves the unneeded gate OPEN — JoinNode's documented straggler-cancellation gap, and the reason a late reject can still fail a run whose write has landed
